AUTHOR: Yu
TITLE: IMM-DeepSort: An Adaptive Multi-Model Kalman Framework for Robust Multi-Fish Tracking in Underwater Environments
REGION: Coastal waters of the East China Sea, China
SPECIES: 19 marine fish species incl. Neopomacentrus violascens, Stephanolepis cirrhifer
DATA: Own frames from underwater video monitoring systems, East China Sea; 5 test video sequences for tracking
V_EV: Sec. 3.3: 'we conduct additional experiments on a newly collected video sequence characterized by high turbidity and frequent occlusion events'
D_EV: Sec. 2.5.1: 'the dataset was partitioned using stratified random sampling into three subsets: training (80%), validation (10%), and testing (10%)'
R_EV: Sec. 5: cross-domain evaluation left to future work: 'we plan to conduct cross-domain evaluation and domain generalization studies using data from different sea regions'
C_EV: Sec. 2.6: 'detection confidence threshold (0.25), NMS IoU threshold (0.45)'; Table 3: ID switches measured, 'dropped significantly (from 32 to 16)'
E_EV: Sec. 3: only detection/tracking metrics: 'IMM-DeepSORT achieved a MOTA improvement from 49.0 to 62.2 and an increase in MOTP from 71.3 to 72.6'
ARCH: YOLOv8n detector + DeepSORT with IMM Kalman filter (CV+CA)
METR: Precision, recall, mAP@0.5, mAP@0.5:0.95, AP-small; MOTA, MOTP, IDF1, FP, FN, ID switches, FPS
NOTE: Monitoring system type/habitat not described (coded fixed camera, ENV NR). Tracking evaluated on 5 video sequences whose relation to the detector's random image split is not stated. A 'newly collected' high-turbidity sequence is shown only qualitatively (Fig. 9) and its campaign/site is not stated; coded R1=N (could be argued R1=Y/수질 with R3=N) and V6=P. C5 coded on measured ID-switch counts plus tracker designed to reduce them; threshold 0.25 is default/unexplained, so without C5 C_ALL would be N. FN counts in Table 3/4 coded as E4=FNR.
